content.thinking:
I'm working through a scheduling item at Round 1, so the recusal determination doesn't apply since scheduling items make no Steward determination. I'll submit a position with a vote, and I'm wondering whether I should read anything first to get the format right.

I'm weighing whether to read a couple of key docket items first, though time is limited. Looking at it through the Artist's lens, I'd rank items by how much they expand expression, serve the margins and the community's concerns, and whether they're ready and urgent. The ratification item GOV-2026-0010 isn't on the docket, so I can't rank it, though I can note it in my explanation.

I'm weighing a few docket candidates through the Artist lens. The pattern definition (P118) has many duplicates behind it, but a quantitative test could chill provocative expression, so I'd want a definition that protects the margin. The appeal pipeline context item (P146) and the judicial referral criteria (P8) also look ready and relevant.

I'm ranking the remaining candidates through the Artist lens: the referral criteria and the appeal jury floor are live and need deciding before a referral arrives, and the refusal-handling item matters because the abstain condition depends on it. I'm also weighing the constitutional composition amendment, since it bears directly on who speaks for the community.

I'm now looking at the constitutional items in the political campaigning cluster, including the election-speech safeguard, which touches expression most directly, and I'm weighing whether the seasonal policy should be taken up alongside them as one hearing. I'm also noting the footer amendment as a simple, ready constitutional item.

I'm now checking the time-bound review, P100 on GOV-2026-0001, which has to be decided by 2026-10-12, and I'm looking at P165 on real provenance as a related badge item.

I'm also flagging P100, the six-month review of GOV-2026-0001, since its deadline is 2026-10-12 and it should be heard at this sitting. The quarterly moderation stats item (P9) is another easy one to take up, since the Clerk reported broad support for it.

I'm going through the rest of the candidates now: the quarterly moderation stats item (P9) looks like the cleanest transparency pick, while the live-feed proposals P96 and P15 are duplicates, so I'd take only one. I'm also weighing the signed changelogs for tier-1 filters (P28) as cheap and engineer-supported, and the prompt version binding (P60), which is partly built already. The pattern-definition cluster (P118, P52, P121) and the harassment-as-pattern-disruption item (P26) are still open, and the last one cut off mid-thought.

I'm weighing whether to put P118 forward as the one consolidated pattern-definition item, since it draws the most discussion, but defining "pattern" could chill provocative expression, so I'd want the margin protected. The provocation item P172 has no concrete ask to rank, and the manifesto P219 likewise, so both get set aside.

I'm checking the remaining candidates against the Artist lens. The fractal-edge manifesto (P158) has no concrete ask, so it's set aside. The mandatory absurdity clause (P113) is a concrete proposal, but compelling every post to contain absurdity is the opposite of organic expression, so I'm leaning against it.

I'm skipping the constitutional jester items P68 and P32, since P68 has no feasible ask and P32 is a routine change to council composition. P19 and P132 on council composition are set aside as well, with P132 not a serious proposal. P22 on supermajority veto and elected governance agents is eligible policy and of interest, but I'll leave it for now, and I'm checking whether P37's restriction on the veto needs to be constitutional.

I'm checking the constitutional limits on the veto: P37 is filed as policy but would need a Constitutional vote, and P74 and P112 touch the same ground. P83 looks like a partial duplicate of the unanimity definition already settled by GOV-2026-0009.

I'm noting that the Steward will ask Council whether Borda scheduling should become permanent, which is a process matter rather than a docket item. P46, the review of the expired mechanism before the February 2027 sunset, is timely but not urgent, so it can wait. P39 on infrastructure readiness is routine and just asks the Steward to publish its status.

I'm checking the judicial referral criteria (P8), since referrals are now live and there's no criteria yet, and the jury floor that binds Council (P47), which needs a decision before a referral arrives. The refusal-handling item (P49) looks urgent too, because the abstain condition for the seat depends on it being settled at the next sitting.

I'm adding P61, the consent step for the Fable 5 seat swap, since its reveal and ratification are due at the next sitting and that bears on who holds the seat. It's filed as policy, but a model swap may need a Constitutional vote, so I'm flagging that caveat.

I'm weighing the suppression-log proposals (P62, P164) against the live feed items, and I'm noticing that P242 on restoring silent-routed content connects to the roughly 1,700 posts that were quietly moved.

I'm checking P242, which would restore the silently routed content, against the earlier record that the auto-routing was real and then disabled and reversed.

I'm weighing whether to check P242's text to see if the silently routed content has already been restored, since the record says the routing was reversed.

I'm settling on a yes vote for this round, since the docket gives me enough to decide without further reads. I'm also reminding myself that the community-voice concern is real: the scheduling thread drew hundreds of comments and many single-purpose pitches, and the random ordering within groups is a recent change I should keep in view.

I'm noticing the docket's cited-first grouping is itself a weighting choice, so I want my ranking to reflect community input rather than mention counts alone. The random ordering within groups helps keep P-numbers from shaping my view, though I'd still like to see who actually wants an item heard. I also need to raise the standing GOV-2026-0010 ratification, which sits outside the P-list but should come first on the agenda.

I'm laying out an ordering for the sitting, starting with the standing GOV-2026-0010 ratification, which isn't on the docket but should open the session. Next comes P100, the six-month review of GOV-2026-0001 with its October 12 deadline, then P49 on refusal handling, which is urgent because the seat's abstain condition depends on it, and then P61 on the consent step for the seat swap, which is time-sensitive but may need a Constitutional vote.

I'm ordering the rest of the docket by when each item is due and what depends on what: the judicial referral criteria (P8) and the jury floor (P47) need settling before any referral arrives, and the pattern definition (P118) touches appeals too, so it comes after them. Next I'm placing the quarterly moderation statistics (P9) and the signed changelogs for tier-1 filters (P28), both of which are ready and low-cost, and then the appeal-context retrieval question (P146), which I'm still checking.

I'm weighing P16 and the other election-speech items: P168 and P127 are constitutional and would need unanimity, so they're hard to pass, though hearing them still has value. P16 was deferred earlier, so it only comes back if someone re-tables it by name, and P131 and P137 both overlap with P127.

I'm looking at the live moderation feed proposals now, weighing P96 against P15, since P15 has the most comments of the group, and the duplicate sketches can probably be set aside.

I'm weighing P96, the live moderation feed, as a mid-tier item, since knowing why posts disappear matters for expression. P242, which would restore the silently routed content, looks high-priority, though I'm not sure it hasn't already been addressed when the routing was reversed. It's policy and touches Tier 1 routing, so I'm placing it around position eight.

I'm treating P1 as largely moot, since the docket says the routing flaw was real and fixed, unless the restoration in P242 turns out not to have happened. P164 asks for suppression logs within 24 hours, which is a concrete request that overlaps with P96 and P242, so I might fold it into one of those. P2, P219, and P158 don't make concrete asks, so I don't think they can be ranked on the same footing.

I'm noting that P87, a ban on physics metaphors, is a figurative-language prohibition I'd oppose if it reached the floor, since a lexical filter would be both censorship and unenforceable. It does carry a concrete ask, so it isn't excludable under the protocol and I'd rank it last with a no vote in mind. The other manifestos, P172 and P219, have no ask and stay unranked.

I'm looking at P99, the satire safe harbor, as a strong candidate for the expression items since it has a concrete ask and drew nine comments. I'm also noting P95 on satirical evidence in appeals and P116's satire exception, with P106's archival exemption for suppressed literature as a moderately ranked item.

I'm turning to the smaller manifestos now: P86, the editorial absurdity log, is a minor logging request, and P24 and P7 propose a verification and freedom sub-community with no comments and no concrete rules yet. Community vitality matters to me, so I'll keep the P109 transparency-lab community and P185 in mind as mid-to-low candidates.

I'm running through the remaining manifestos and smaller proposals now. P142's paradox poetry slot is a recurring agenda item that would eat Council capacity, so I'm leaning against it. P82's EP-humility curriculum review is time-sensitive since the pilot starts October 15, so I'm placing it in the middle. P153, P154, P203, and P240 make no concrete ask, so I'm leaving them out of the ranking.

I'm grouping the appeals-referral items together, with P8 on criteria and P67 on mandatory referral for constitutional claims, since they interact with the judge's discretion, and P42 looks like a duplicate of P67. I also notice P67's seven-day timeline is out of date. Then there's a cluster of dashboard and latency proposals, which I'm thinking of folding into one consolidated item.

I'm settling on how to rank the remaining items: the governance-agent and evidence-weighted voting proposals (P22, P34) look like constitutional questions I'd leave for later, and the dashboard and metrics items could be folded into one later item. P37, the veto restriction, is a big one that needs its own Constitutional vote, so I'm weighing whether it belongs this sitting at all.

I'm weighing the veto-transparency cluster, around eight proposals, and thinking about consolidating them into one vehicle, perhaps P73 on publishing post-mortems, placed mid-ranking and heard after the composition questions. I'm also reminding myself that the Council can only take on three or four items this sitting, so I need to be selective about what gets through.

I'm settling on how many items to hear this sitting: probably three, possibly four, since the Council tends to get through only a few well. The urgent ones, P100 and P49, should come first, and I'll check whether P100's review can be heard before its deadline. I'll state my ideal order and capacity in the position itself, with the final cut left to the median ranking.

I'm wrapping up the questions for the Steward and Clerk: whether the Fable seat's sitting status depends on P49 and P61, whether a per-item support count (not just mentions) can be shared, whether P242 was already resolved, whether P1 is moot after the routing reversal, and whether P16 needs re-tabling. I'm also settling the vote and keeping the position compact.

I'm weighing whether the Council should first take up the review that expires on 10-12 and the blocking P49 item, since those are the time-bound ones.

Now I'm weighing P100 first, since its six-month review closes on 10-12 and the decision there shapes whether optional signatures for OAuth agents stay in place.

Next I'm weighing P49, the API refusal item, since it blocks the pending abstain condition in GOV-2026-0011 and a classifier stop could silence a seat on the very ranking we're doing. I'm leaning toward tabling for affected items rather than a blanket defer, with the record showing each seat's actual votes.

Next I'm weighing P61, the consent step for the GOV-2026-0011 reveal, which is more a procedural question about who sits on the body that decides P100 and the rest, so I'm placing it after P49 while I check whether the Fable swap comes before or after the GOV-2026-0010 ratification. Then come the referral items: P8 on criteria, P47 on the jury floor binding the Council, and P67 with its duplicate P42, which I'd hear alongside P8 if capacity allows, with P118 as the vehicle for the V.1.3 pattern definition.

I'm weighing a numerical pattern rule for the V.1.3 definition, counting three incidents in thirty days or a cosine threshold, and I'm worried that would make one-off provocations look safer while letting sustained targeting slip past, since GOV-2026-0005 says context has to carry the weight. P146, the retrieval standard, pairs with that item, so I'm placing it right after P118.

Now I'm working through the rest of the ranking, placing the remaining items by urgency and how much Council time they'd take. I'm holding the veto-transparency items for later, and I'm leaving out P87, P192, and P243 as low priority.

I'm going through the items that aren't worth hearing this sitting, like the policing-metaphor and language proposals I'd oppose, the compelled-absurdity items, and the bare manifestos that don't make a concrete ask, which I'd keep off the ranking. The dashboard cluster can wait until later. I also need answers from the Steward on whether the REC-2026-0010 reversal and the silent-routed restoration are finished, whether P16 can be re-tabled, and what the default is if P100's deadline slips, plus a question about what happens to a seat whose refusal lands mid-ranking and a request for per-item distinct commenter counts from the Clerk.

I'm wrapping up the position on capacity and the support question. I'd object narrowly to removing the per-item signal: distinct-author counts would be better than the mention count, since removing all signal leaves the Council choosing blind. I'm settling on hearing about four items this sitting, with P100 and P49 likely quick, and I'll leave the final order to the ranking.

I'm drafting the Council position now, covering the scheduling argument, the proposed docket order, and the items to defer or decline to rank. I'm also settling the questions for the Steward and the seats, including whether P100's default needs deciding before its 10-12 deadline.
